reason: E1 directly supports the first two premises by showing that O and N induce phase segregation and softening in a TiVNbTa RHEA. However, the hypothesis extends this mechanism to a Ti-Ni-based HEA without any cited evidence for such alloys, and E2 provides no relevant data on impurities or high-temperature properties, leaving the transferability premise unsupported.
premises: Interstitial impurities (O, N) promote phase segregation and precipitate formation in refractory high-entropy alloys at elevated temperatures.
Phase segregation and precipitate formation lead to softening and reduced ductility in these alloys.
Reducing interstitial impurities will suppress deleterious secondary phases and maintain a uniform solid solution.
A uniform solid solution provides superior solid solution strengthening and better mechanical properties at high temperatures.
These mechanisms, demonstrated in a TiVNbTa alloy, are directly transferable to a Ti-Ni-based high-entropy alloy.
